attachments.title: Source clinical note
attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-11-15
Provider: Dr. Marcus Rodriguez, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Headache, low-grade fever, and nausea for two days with recent exposure to summer camp outbreak.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient is a 9-year-old male last seen in January 2020 for routine care with sedentary lifestyle concerns. He presents with headache, low-grade fever, nausea for past 2 days. Parents report he has been less active than usual, preferring to lie in a dark room. He has had no vomiting, seizures, or confusion. Recently attended summer camp where multiple other children developed similar symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Long-distance running (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Noncontributory

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: Elementary school student.

VITAL SIGNS:
A low-grade fever (38.1°C)

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Physical examination reveals photophobia, and mild neck stiffness with resistance to passive neck flexion. Brudzinski and Kernig signs are both positive.

LABORATORY DATA:
CSF Gram stain is negative. Viral PCR is pending

IMAGING:
A non-contrast CT scan of the head is unremarkable

OTHER STUDIES:
A lumbar puncture is performed

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:
The clinical picture is consistent with echovirus infection

attachments.title: Source clinical note
attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Pediatrics
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Routine annual check-up before starting a new school year with maternal concern regarding sedentary lifestyle and excessive video game use.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The mother expresses concern about her son's sedentary lifestyle, noting that he spends most of his time playing video games after school and has little interest in physical activities. She reports that he has a healthy diet but is worried about his lack of exercise.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
The boy has no significant medical history and is up-to-date with his vaccinations.

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Noncontributory

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: Elementary school student.

VITAL SIGNS:
On examination, the child's height and weight are at the 50th percentile for his age. His blood pressure is 110/70 mmHg, heart rate is 78 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
The physical examination is unremarkable.

PLAN:
The pediatrician decides to discuss exercise recommendations with the mother and her son.
